agencies.name: Police Department
agencies.desc: Patrol, detective, traffic enforcement, counterterrorism, and school safety across NYC's five boroughs. The largest municipal police force in the US.

agencies.name: Fire Department
agencies.desc: Fire suppression, emergency medical services (EMS), hazmat response, and fire prevention inspections citywide.

agencies.name: Department of Correction
agencies.desc: Operates the city jail system including Rikers Island and borough facilities. Responsible for the custody and care of pretrial detainees.

agencies.name: Department of Probation
agencies.desc: Supervises adults and juveniles on probation; operates the NeON centers providing job training and youth services in high-incarceration neighborhoods.

agencies.name: Civilian Complaint Review Board
agencies.desc: Independent city agency that investigates, mediates, and prosecutes complaints against NYPD officers. Has authority to recommend discipline.

agencies.name: Office of Admin Trials & Hearings
agencies.desc: Administrative court handling hearings for city agencies including DOB violations, taxi and food vendor adjudications, and employee disciplinary cases.

agencies.name: Department of Investigation
agencies.desc: Inspector general for NYC government. Investigates corruption, fraud, and misconduct by city employees, contractors, and officials.

agencies.name: Conflicts of Interest Board
agencies.desc: Enforces NYC's conflicts of interest laws for city employees and elected officials. Issues guidance and investigates violations.

agencies.name: Office of Emergency Management
agencies.desc: Coordinates city agencies and community partners to prepare for, respond to, and recover from disasters and large-scale emergencies.

agencies.name: Department of Education
agencies.desc: Operates the largest school district in the US — 1,600+ schools serving over 900,000 students. Includes funding from city, state, and federal sources.

agencies.name: City University of New York
agencies.desc: 25-campus public university system serving 230,000+ degree students. Includes flagship colleges (City, Brooklyn, Hunter, Queens) and 7 community colleges.

agencies.name: School Construction Authority
agencies.desc: Plans, manages, and implements construction, renovation, and modernization of NYC public schools. Oversees multi-billion-dollar capital plan.

agencies.name: New York Public Library
agencies.desc: City-funded nonprofit library system serving Manhattan, the Bronx, and Staten Island. 92 branches, plus the flagship research libraries on 42nd St.

agencies.name: Brooklyn Public Library
agencies.desc: Independent public library system serving all of Brooklyn's 2.6 million residents across 60 branches.

agencies.name: Queens Public Library
agencies.desc: Serves Queens across 65 branches with one of the largest immigrant-serving programs of any library system in the country.

agencies.name: Human Resources Administration
agencies.desc: Administers SNAP (food stamps), Medicaid enrollment, cash assistance, domestic violence services, and adult protective services. NYC's social safety net backbone.

agencies.name: Department of Homeless Services
agencies.desc: Provides emergency shelter for adults, families, and youth experiencing homelessness. Operates the citywide shelter system and outreach programs.

agencies.name: NYC Health + Hospitals
agencies.desc: Nation's largest municipal health system — 11 hospitals, over 70 community health centers and clinics, serving 1.1 million New Yorkers annually, regardless of ability to pay.

agencies.name: Administration for Children's Svcs
agencies.desc: Child welfare agency responsible for child protective services, foster care, preventive services, and juvenile justice programs.

agencies.name: Dept of Health & Mental Hygiene
agencies.desc: Public health agency overseeing disease surveillance, mental health licensing, restaurant inspections, vital records, and community health initiatives.

agencies.name: Department for the Aging
agencies.desc: Funds and oversees a network of senior centers, home-delivered meals, caregiver support, legal services, and other programs for NYC's 1.6 million older adults.

agencies.name: Youth & Community Development
agencies.desc: Funds community-based organizations providing after-school programs, summer youth jobs, adult literacy, and immigration services citywide.

agencies.name: Housing Preservation & Development
agencies.desc: Finances affordable housing construction and preservation, enforces housing quality standards, and oversees tenant protection. NYC's primary affordable housing agency.

agencies.name: NYC Housing Authority
agencies.desc: Operates 177,000 public housing apartments across 300+ developments, housing over 300,000 low-income New Yorkers. One of the largest public housing authorities in the US.

agencies.name: Department of City Planning
agencies.desc: Prepares the city's comprehensive land use plan, manages the ULURP review process, and leads neighborhood rezonings including recent City of Yes for Housing Opportunity.

agencies.name: Landmarks Preservation Commission
agencies.desc: Designates and regulates NYC's 38,000+ landmarked properties — individual landmarks, interior landmarks, scenic landmarks, and 152 historic districts.

agencies.name: Department of Transportation
agencies.desc: Maintains and improves the city's 6,300 miles of streets, 789 bridges, 12,000 intersections, and manages cycling infrastructure, parking regulation, and ferry operations.

agencies.name: Dept of Environmental Protection
agencies.desc: Manages the city's water supply (1.1 billion gallons/day), wastewater treatment, 14 reservoirs, and enforces air and noise pollution regulations.

agencies.name: Dept of Design & Construction
agencies.desc: City's primary capital project delivery agency — manages construction of public buildings, infrastructure, and roadways for other agencies.

agencies.name: Department of Sanitation
agencies.desc: Collects 12,000 tons of refuse daily, operates composting and recycling programs, and clears snow from 6,400 miles of streets during winter storms.

agencies.name: Dept of Citywide Admin Services
agencies.desc: Manages city real estate, government procurement, vehicle fleet (26,000 vehicles), citywide civil service testing, and energy purchasing.

agencies.name: Department of Finance
agencies.desc: Collects city taxes ($35B+ annually), manages property valuation for 1 million+ properties, enforces parking and camera violations, and administers tax relief programs.

agencies.name: Office of Management & Budget
agencies.desc: Prepares and manages the city's $118B annual budget, tracks spending, and coordinates fiscal policy across all agencies.

agencies.name: Office of Technology & Innovation
agencies.desc: Manages citywide IT infrastructure including NYC.gov, broadband expansion, 311 systems, and cybersecurity. Oversees broadband access initiatives.

agencies.name: Law Department
agencies.desc: Serves as the City's law firm — represents NYC in litigation, advises agencies on legal matters, and handles labor negotiations.

agencies.name: Office of Payroll Administration
agencies.desc: Processes payroll for over 300,000 city employees across all agencies and pension funds.

agencies.name: Mayor's Office of Contract Services
agencies.desc: Oversees the city's $20B+ contracting process, administers PASSPort (city's online procurement system), and ensures compliance with procurement rules.

agencies.name: Dept of Records & Info Services
agencies.desc: Manages the NYC Municipal Archives, the City Record (official newspaper), FOIL requests, and preservation of city records.

agencies.name: Department of Parks & Recreation
agencies.desc: Maintains 30,000 acres of parkland, 800+ playgrounds, 14 miles of beaches, 35 recreation centers, and hundreds of ball fields across the five boroughs.

agencies.name: Department of Cultural Affairs
agencies.desc: Funds and supports 1,000+ cultural organizations citywide including museums, theaters, dance companies, and arts education programs. Manages 33 city-owned cultural buildings.

agencies.name: Small Business Services
agencies.desc: Supports businesses and workers through NYC Business Solutions centers, Workforce1 career centers, minority/women-owned business certification, and Industrial Business Zones.

agencies.name: Economic Development Corporation
agencies.desc: City's primary economic development engine — manages city-owned real estate, develops large projects (Willets Point, Sunnyside Yard), and supports industry sectors.

agencies.name: Department of Buildings
agencies.desc: Issues construction permits, inspects buildings for code compliance, and enforces the NYC Building Code across 1 million+ buildings.

agencies.name: Consumer & Worker Protection
agencies.desc: Licenses businesses (75,000+ licenses), enforces consumer protection laws, adjudicates wage theft claims, and administers the paid safe and sick leave law.

agencies.name: Taxi & Limousine Commission
agencies.desc: Licenses and regulates 80,000+ for-hire vehicles — yellow and green taxis, black cars, liveries, and Uber/Lyft FHVs — plus their 200,000+ drivers.

agencies.name: Business Integrity Commission
agencies.desc: Regulates the commercial waste industry and public wholesale markets to prevent organized crime and ensure fair competition. Oversees 100+ trade waste companies.

agencies.name: Office of the Comptroller
agencies.desc: Independent elected official who audits city agencies, manages $280B pension fund assets, approves city contracts, and investigates fiscal misconduct.

agencies.name: Public Advocate
agencies.desc: Elected city ombudsman who investigates complaints about city agencies, proposes legislation, and serves as next in line to the mayor.

agencies.name: City Council
agencies.desc: NYC's 51-member legislative body — passes the city budget, enacts local laws, and exercises oversight over the mayoral agencies. Speaker leads Council operations.

agencies.name: Manhattan Borough President
agencies.desc: Elected official representing Manhattan's 1.6 million residents. Advises the mayor and city council on land use, capital priorities, and local policy.

agencies.name: Brooklyn Borough President
agencies.desc: Elected official representing Brooklyn's 2.6 million residents — the most populous borough. Coordinates land use advisory and capital needs.

agencies.name: Queens Borough President
agencies.desc: Elected official representing Queens' 2.3 million residents — the most ethnically diverse urban county in the world.

agencies.name: Bronx Borough President
agencies.desc: Elected official representing the Bronx's 1.4 million residents. Focuses heavily on housing and environmental justice issues.

agencies.name: Staten Island Borough President
agencies.desc: Elected official representing Staten Island's 490,000 residents — NYC's least densely populated borough.

agencies.name: District Attorney — Manhattan
agencies.desc: Elected prosecutor for New York County (Manhattan). Prosecutes felonies and misdemeanors, and investigates white-collar crime, financial fraud, and public corruption.

agencies.name: District Attorney — Brooklyn
agencies.desc: Elected prosecutor for Kings County (Brooklyn). Second-largest DA office in the country by caseload.

agencies.name: District Attorney — Queens
agencies.desc: Elected prosecutor for Queens County. Handles one of the most ethnically and linguistically diverse caseloads in the country.

agencies.name: District Attorney — Bronx
agencies.desc: Elected prosecutor for Bronx County. Implements significant restorative justice and diversion programs.

agencies.name: District Attorney — Staten Island
agencies.desc: Elected prosecutor for Richmond County (Staten Island).

agencies.name: Board of Elections
agencies.desc: Administers all federal, state, and local elections in NYC — including voter registration, early voting, absentee ballots, poll site operations, and candidate filings.

agencies.name: Commission on Human Rights
agencies.desc: Enforces the NYC Human Rights Law — one of the most expansive anti-discrimination laws in the nation — covering employment, housing, and public accommodations.
